title: Global View - New Years Resolution

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine and today we're talking about something we talk about every year.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们正在谈论我们每年谈论的事情。

segments.en: Every year after Christmas or well during the Christmas holidays, we talk about New Years, New Years Day and a very important topic, New Years Resolutions.
segments.zh: 每年圣诞节期间或圣诞节过后，我们都会谈论新年、元旦，以及一个非常重要的话题——新年决心。

segments.en: Alright, so we're not going to preview anything today.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们今天不打算预览任何东西。

segments.en: It's all in the dialogue but when we come back, we'll be talking more about what you hear and some of the great phrases you can use at the New Year.
segments.zh: 这一切都在对话中，但当我们回来时，我们会更多地谈论你听到的内容以及你可以在新年使用的一些很棒的短语。

segments.en: Did you read this?
segments.zh: 你看过这个了吗？

segments.en: It says that the number one New Year resolution people make is to spend more time with friends and family.
segments.zh: 上面说，人们最常许下的新年愿望，就是多花点时间陪亲友。

segments.en: Why would that be funny?
segments.zh: 为什么会很有趣？

segments.en: Well think about it.
segments.zh: 你好好想想。

segments.en: We are a society that is always on the go.
segments.zh: 如今这个社会，大家总是忙个不停。

segments.en: Not because we have to but because we want to.
segments.zh: 不是因为我们必须这样做，而是因为我们想要。

segments.en: Why?
segments.zh: 为什么？

segments.en: We work hard and spend less time at home because we are trying to provide for our family with goods and services that are usually unnecessary.
segments.zh: 我们努力工作，在家中花费的时间更少，因为我们试图为我们的家人提供通常不必要的商品和服务。

segments.en: I don't agree but anyways, I think you should start thinking of a New Year's resolution yourself.
segments.zh: 我不同意，但无论如何，我认为你应该自己开始考虑新年的决心。

segments.en: What's the point?
segments.zh: 这有什么意义？

segments.en: We always make New Year's resolutions and by February, we will have forgotten about them.
segments.zh: 我们总是制定新年的决心，到二月，我们会忘记它们。

segments.en: It's pointless.
segments.zh: 这毫无意义。

segments.en: Well maybe then you should resolve to sticking to your goals and objectives.
segments.zh: 那你干脆下定决心，坚持完成自己定下的目标吧。

segments.en: What about you?
segments.zh: 你呢？

segments.en: Your gym bag is gathering dust and you still have brand new running shoes that are yet to be jogged in.
segments.zh: 你的健身包都落灰了，那双全新的跑鞋还一次都没穿着跑过呢。

segments.en: Well I would go if you kept your promise of going to the gym with me every day.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你遵守每天和我一起去健身房的承诺，我会去的。

segments.en: Yeah, yeah, whatever.
segments.zh: 好好好，随你怎么说。

segments.en: Alright, great, we're back.
segments.zh: 好吧，太好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So this is very typical.
segments.zh: 所以这是非常典型的。

segments.en: A New Year's resolution that you make but then people don't really stick to it, etc.
segments.zh: 你制定的新年决心，但人们并没有真正坚持下去，等等。

segments.en: They don't?
segments.zh: 他们没有？

segments.en: Usually they don't.
segments.zh: 通常他们不会。

segments.en: Alright, but you're probably wondering what is a New Year's resolution so why don't we take a look at this word and many more on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 好吧，你可能想知道什么是新年决心，那我们来看看这个词，以及语言要点里的更多内容。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: Okay, so New Year's resolution, let's break this phrase down.
segments.zh: 好的，所以新年的决心，让我们分解一下这句话。

segments.en: The first phrase is New Year's.
segments.zh: 第一句话是新年。

segments.en: So the New Year is January 1st in the West and it is celebrated on the 31st of December at night when the clock changes to the New Year and a New Year's resolution, remember that S there, is something that you want to do or to change in the New Year.
segments.zh: 所以新年在西方是 1 月 1 日，人们在 12 月 31 日晚上庆祝，那时时钟跨入新年。而 New Year's resolution（注意这里有个 s）就是你想在新的一年里做或改变的事情。

segments.en: It's a fresh start.
segments.zh: 这是一个新的开始。

segments.en: Okay, so you pretty much, the verb that you use there is to resolve to do something.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以基本上，这里用到的动词是 resolve，表示下定决心做某事。

segments.en: So my New Year's resolution is to go to the gym every day.
segments.zh: 所以我的新年决心是每天去健身房。

segments.en: It's like a promise to yourself.
segments.zh: 这就像对自己的承诺。

segments.en: Right, so and this is very common right among Americans.
segments.zh: 是的，所以这在美国人中很常见。

segments.en: They try and because it's a New Year, it's a fresh start so they want to start doing something great.
segments.zh: 他们尝试，因为这是新的一年，这是一个新的开始，所以他们想开始做一些伟大的事情。

segments.en: Exactly, we can talk about this at the end but a lot of companies try to use this to sell Americans stupid things so we'll get there in a minute.
segments.zh: 没错，这个我们最后再聊，但很多公司想借这个向美国人推销些没用的东西，所以这个我们待会儿再说。

segments.en: But the two people in this dialogue are talking about the idea of spending more time with friends and family.
segments.zh: 但这次对话中的两个人正在谈论花更多时间与朋友和家人在一起的想法。

segments.en: And the other person says, well sometimes it's hard to do that because you have to provide your family with goods and services.
segments.zh: 另一个人说，有时很难做到这一点，因为你必须为你的家人提供商品和服务。

segments.en: This phrase goods and services is very common especially in economics and sociology.
segments.zh: goods and services 这个短语非常常见，尤其是在经济学和社会学中。

segments.en: So what does this mean?
segments.zh: 那么，这是什么意思？

segments.en: And they go together, right?
segments.zh: 它们总是连在一起用，对吧？

segments.en: So goods are tangible items, things that you buy, you know like food or you know clothes, a TV, etc.
segments.zh: 所以 goods 是有形的物品，就是你买的东西，比如食物、衣服、电视等等。

segments.en: Stuff.
segments.zh: 东西。

segments.en: Stuff.
segments.zh: 东西。

segments.en: And services of course are other things like for example going to the doctor or the dentist or any other service you get.
segments.zh: 当然，服务是其他事情，例如去看医生或牙医或您获得的任何其他服务。

segments.en: So service usually includes another person doing something for you.
segments.zh: 所以服务通常包括另一个人为你做某事。

segments.en: But you might not actually get something physical like a TV if you pay for it.
segments.zh: 但你花钱买服务时，实际并不会得到像电视那样的实物。

segments.en: So goods and services, it's included in this phrase always goods and services.
segments.zh: 所以 goods and services，这个短语里总是两个词一起出现。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And well moving on as we mentioned with the New Year's resolution, we had that verb there, to resolve.
segments.zh: 好，接下来，刚才提到新年决心时，我们看到了那个动词——resolve。

segments.en: So what does it mean if I want to resolve?
segments.zh: 那如果我想下定决心，它是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Okay well to resolve as we said is to decide or to promise yourself to do something.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如我们说的，resolve 就是决定或向自己承诺去做某事。

segments.en: So it's a decision that you don't want to change your mind about.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个你不想改变主意的决定。

segments.en: For example, I, this year, I've resolved to quit smoking.
segments.zh: 例如，我，今年，我决定戒烟。

segments.en: That means I've made a decision for myself and I'm going to do it.
segments.zh: 这意味着我已经为自己做出了决定，我会去做的。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: It's very strong.
segments.zh: 它非常强大。

segments.en: And not to be confused with like to solve, right?
segments.zh: 别把它和 solve 搞混了，对吧？

segments.en: It has no real relation there, right?
segments.zh: 它在那里没有真正的关系，对吧？

segments.en: No, resolve, to resolve to do something is to have a strong passion or interest in doing something for yourself or changing an action.
segments.zh: 不，决心，决心做某事是对为自己做某事或改变行动有强烈的热情或兴趣。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And well our last word for language takeaway is brand new.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们对语言要点的最后一个词是全新的。

segments.en: A brand new, something that's brand new.
segments.zh: 一个全新的，全新的东西。

segments.en: Brand new, so buy a brand new car.
segments.zh: 全新，所以买一辆全新的汽车。

segments.en: Come down to Captain's car lot.
segments.zh: 快来 Captain 车行看看。

segments.en: So brand new is something we hear a lot in marketing.
segments.zh: brand new 这个词我们在营销中经常听到。

segments.en: It's also something that, well these words just go together very often.
segments.zh: 而且这两个词经常搭配在一起。

segments.en: And something is new, okay, you just bought it or it just came out.
segments.zh: 有些东西是新的，好吧，你刚买了，或者它刚刚出来。

segments.en: But something that's brand new is really fresh, really new.
segments.zh: 但是全新的东西真的很新鲜，真的很新。

segments.en: So brand new, a brand new car, a brand new watch, etc.
segments.zh: 所以 brand new，一辆全新的汽车、一块全新的手表等等。

segments.en: A brand new movie.
segments.zh: 一部全新的电影。

segments.en: A brand new movie or brand new cereal.
segments.zh: 一部全新的电影或全新的谷物。

segments.en: Have you ever tried it?
segments.zh: 你试过吗？

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So great phrases there.
segments.zh: 那里有这么棒的短语。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So great words there.
segments.zh: 那里有这么棒的词。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase is very common at gas stations and fast food chains.
segments.zh: 好吧，这第一个短语在加油站和快餐连锁店很常见。

segments.en: We say on the go.
segments.zh: 我们说的是 on the go。

segments.en: Alright, so he mentioned that we are a society that is always on the go.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以他提到我们是一个永远在路上的社会。

segments.en: It means we're always moving.
segments.zh: 这意味着我们总是在移动。

segments.en: Exactly, so you're always going to work, going home from work, going to the store, going to the school to get the kids.
segments.zh: 没错，所以你总是去上班，下班回家，去商店，去学校接孩子。

segments.en: Always moving, moving, moving.
segments.zh: 总是移动，移动，移动。

segments.en: So that kind of action, that kind of life is on the go.
segments.zh: 所以那种行动，那种生活在路上。

segments.en: You can also say eat on the go.
segments.zh: 你也可以说在旅途中吃饭。

segments.en: That means I eat while I'm going somewhere, while I'm doing something.
segments.zh: 意思是我一边赶路、一边做事的时候吃东西。

segments.en: I don't sit down.
segments.zh: 我不坐下。

segments.en: Okay, so on the go.
segments.zh: 好吧，那么在旅途中。

segments.en: And well, talking about New Year's resolution and we said that well many people resolve to do something but they don't really do it.
segments.zh: 好吧，谈到新年的决心，我们说很多人决心做某事，但他们并没有真正做到这一点。

segments.en: And we have a phrase that is used here, to stick to something.
segments.zh: 这里用到的短语是 to stick to something。

segments.en: Stick to your resolution.
segments.zh: 坚持你的决心。

segments.en: To stick to it.
segments.zh: 坚持下去。

segments.en: So you think of tape or glue, these things that help things stick together.
segments.zh: 所以你会想到胶带或胶水，它们能让东西粘在一起。

segments.en: Okay, so in that sense it's kind of a way for you to describe continuing to do something or not stopping, not quitting, not ending it.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以从这个意义上说，这是一种让你描述继续做某事或不停止、不放弃、不结束它的方式。

segments.en: And so I could say, remember how I said I wanted to quit smoking?

segments.en: Well I'm really going to stick to this resolution because I think it's important.

segments.en: That means I'm not going to give up.

segments.en: Right, very good.

segments.en: So you're going to stay with it.

segments.en: And we could say as words of encouragement, hey stick to it.

segments.en: Alright, this is a very nice phrase I think because it's very visual.
segments.zh: 好吧，我认为这是一个非常好的短语，因为它非常直观。

segments.en: I like phrases where you can see what's happening.
segments.zh: 我喜欢你可以看到发生了什么的短语。

segments.en: So gathering means collecting.
segments.zh: gathering 就是 collecting，聚集的意思。

segments.en: That means that the dust in the air, it's building on this bag.
segments.zh: 这意味着空气中的灰尘，它在这个袋子上积聚。

segments.en: And something is gathering dust if we don't use it.
segments.zh: 如果我们不使用它，有些东西正在积聚灰尘。

segments.en: So we haven't gone to the gym because our bag is in the corner and it's just filled with dust.
segments.zh: 所以我们还没有去健身房，因为我们的包在角落里，它只是充满了灰尘。

segments.en: Exactly.

segments.en: Very good.

segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: And well, as you mentioned, there are some interesting things about this dialogue, especially when they talked about a society that is always on the go.
segments.zh: 好吧，正如你提到的，这段对话里有几个有意思的点，尤其是他们谈到一个总是忙个不停的社会时。

segments.en: And you mentioned that well, sometimes you eat on the go.
segments.zh: 你提到，有时候你会边赶路边吃东西。

segments.en: And I've seen people in the United States that are actually eating while driving.
segments.zh: 我见过美国人在开车时实际上是在吃东西。

segments.en: I'm guilty of doing that.
segments.zh: 我也干过这种事。

segments.en: Yeah, you have no time to actually sit down for like 15 minutes and eat.
segments.zh: 是啊，你根本没时间真的坐下来花 15 分钟吃顿饭。

segments.en: No, I remember being in high school at home and you just have so much stuff to do.
segments.zh: 不，我记得在家里上高中，你有很多事情要做。

segments.en: You have school, then after school there's like soccer practice, after that there's music lessons and you never have time to eat so you have to grab food in the car and then on the way home you're picking things up and you get home and you do your homework or whatever.
segments.zh: 你要上学，放学后还有足球训练，之后还有音乐课，你永远没时间吃饭，只能在车里随便抓点东西吃，回家路上还得顺路取东西，到家还要写作业什么的。

segments.en: There's so much stuff to do and it doesn't stop.
segments.zh: 有很多事情要做，它不会停止。

segments.en: It doesn't stop when you grow up.
segments.zh: 当你长大后，它不会停止。

segments.en: It doesn't stop if you're an older person.
segments.zh: 如果你是一个年长的人，它不会停止。

segments.en: That's the way life is in America.
segments.zh: 这就是美国生活的方式。

segments.en: Wow, yeah, that's really interesting because I think many of our listeners that are in other countries would find that a little bit peculiar if they actually went to the United States and saw somebody in their car, you know, like having a hamburger while driving, you know, and sipping on their soda.
segments.zh: 哇，是的，这真的很有趣，因为我认为我们在其他国家的许多听众会发现，如果他们真的去美国并看到有人在他们的车里，你知道，就像在开车时吃一个汉堡包，你知道的，他们会发现这有点奇怪。

segments.en: Yeah, it's kind of sad.
segments.zh: 是的，有点难过。

segments.en: Well, that's the thing.
segments.zh: 嗯，就是这样。

segments.en: You don't have much time.
segments.zh: 你没有太多时间。

segments.en: But actually, this is based on true events, kind of, on the fact that many Americans do want to spend more time at home with their friends, with their family because, as you say, you're always so busy.
segments.zh: 但实际上，这是基于真实的事件，某种程度上是因为许多美国人确实想花更多的时间和朋友在一起，和家人在一起，因为，正如你所说，你总是那么忙。

segments.en: And I think it's a nice resolution to resolve to have dinner with your family once or twice a week at home where you sit down and you talk about your lives.
segments.zh: 而且我觉得，下定决心每周在家和家人吃一两次晚饭是个不错的主意，你们可以坐下来聊聊各自的生活。

segments.en: It's nice because you get to share and you get to know each other better and, you know, otherwise you're always just on the go in different places.
segments.zh: 这很好，因为你可以分享，可以更好地了解彼此，否则你们总是忙忙碌碌、各奔东西。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So we want to hear your comments and your opinions about this topic so why don't you visit our website EnglishPod.com and we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 所以我们想听听您对这个话题的评论和意见，所以你为什么不访问我们的网站 englishpod.com，我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Don't forget to share with us your New Year's resolutions.
segments.zh: 不要忘记与我们分享您的新年决心。

segments.en: Everyone's got one.
segments.zh: 每个人都有一个新年决心。

segments.en: So I'm very excited to hear those.
segments.zh: 所以我很高兴听到这些。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Until next time, everyone.
segments.zh: 各位，下次再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Happy New Year.
segments.zh: 新年快乐。
